exercises.notes: **'Four sets of the brutal complex lol it's so hard at 35lbs!!!!'** Went a round past the target at the correct bell — exactly the shape the block was rewritten for after the 50lb opener wrecked it last week. Rounds as the variable, working as designed.

exercises.context: 🛑 Closing skill block — bent press + windmill, light-to-moderate bell, quality over reps.
exercises.notes: *'Bent press + windmill are fine, did at 35.'* Non-event at 35, which is the top of the skill-block range.

shoulderStatus: No flare reported. The fatigue was left-arm specific and read as tiredness, not joint.
lessonsForFutureWeeks: **THE LEFT-ARM CAUSE IS IDENTIFIED AND IT WASN'T PROGRAMMED: super-slow-eccentric KB presses on Tuesday, done 'to mess around.'** He remembered it two days later. That, not the new KB curl, is the likeliest reason the left has been dead all week — slow eccentrics at the top bell are a large unplanned dose, and it landed the day before pull day. **This substantially exonerates the KB curl and it retires the mystery: the W25D3 incline-curl set-one failure has a specific, one-off, self-inflicted cause.** Don't carry 'the left arm is a problem' forward as a standing concern without fresh evidence from a clean week.

**Ad-hoc experiments need to land in the report, because they change the week's readings.** He messed around with slow-eccentric presses on Tuesday and the effect showed up on Wednesday AND Thursday, while three separate theories were being weighed. He agreed: *'i should probably be writing those down more haha.'* Worth asking 'anything you added or played with?' when a reading looks strange.

**THE PUSH-UP GREASING SET IS AT 50 REPS A DAY AND HAS BEEN CLIMBING: 30 → 40 → 50, each step taken when the last got too easy.** At 50 it is ~80% — *'could do more but stopping early'* — so it still satisfies the greasing-the-groove definition, and his read is that *'it doesn't seem to affect push day at all.'* **Leave it. But the program should know it exists:** it is a large daily pressing dose feeding into push day and into every KB day's pressing, and it is the reason the push-up is no longer a warmup-grade movement for him.

**THE LOCKOUT PAUSE FAILED AS AN INTENSITY LEVER — and that's a pass, not a fault.** He ran it correctly and felt nothing: *'i feel like i'm locked out so i don't seem like i'm feeling anything?'* A properly stacked overhead lockout is skeletal, so the hold is the restful part of the press — it audits the position rather than loading it. **Keep it as a short 1s check on the last rep or two, and put the difficulty into tempo levers that can actually carry it:** a 2s pause at the sticking point on the way UP (primary, every set), a pause DOWN at the same height (middle), and a slow 3-4s eccentric on the LAST SET ONLY. **Correction to my first read — slow eccentrics are not off the table; the ad-hoc dose and its timing were the problem, not the method.** 50 is the ceiling bell here, so tempo is this lift's only progression. **Schedule rule: eccentric press work goes on THURSDAY** — Tuesday's overflow lands on pull day, Thursday's lands on legs, which doesn't care.

**HE LADDERED A SECOND FLOW UNPROMPTED — Outside Snatch Flow at 25 / 25 / 35, and 35 was hard.** Same shape as Tuesday's Bent Press Flow ladder. **This is now his default way of running a flow he knows, so write the ladder into familiar-flow blocks rather than a single bell.** Weakest link on the heavy round: **the outside snatch, left side** — *'a reverse iron cross since you're straight arming it into the lockout.'* That's an accurate read of the move: it's the longest straight-arm lever in the flow. Left is where this week's fatigue lived, so don't call it a standing weakness yet.

**KB curl difficulty, revised: harder than a 25lb DB curl, easier than the chest-supported incline curl.** That's a more useful placement than Tuesday's 'didn't feel like it did anything' — it sits in the middle of the curl ladder, which is exactly where a supplementary frequency lift should sit.

**Brutal Complex at 35 got FOUR rounds and read 'so hard.'** The rewrite worked: correct bell, rounds as the variable, and he went past the target under his own steam. Nothing to change. **Bent press + windmill at 35 was a non-event** — top of the skill-block range, no notes.

**FOREARM DIGGING AT 50 — fix the grip, not the wrist.** *'Trying to hold the wrist straight and doing that with a 50lb kb is just wildly digging into the forearm.'* A wrist held straight by effort means the handle is sitting square across the palm, so the bell hangs off the end of the hand and its corner lands on the wrist joint. **The fix is a diagonal, deep grip** — handle running from the base of the index finger to the heel of the hand, aligned with the forearm, hand jammed into the corner of the handle. The bell then rests along the back of the forearm and the wrist goes neutral without being forced. **Some forearm pressure at 50 is the implement, not a fault — digging and bruising is position.** Added to the form-cues doc under C&P.

lessonsForFutureWeeks: **Heaviest squat of the program — 225 total (90/side) on a fourth, unplanned set, and it read effortless.** Built inside the session: 80 × 2 → 85 → 90. **Treat it as a ceiling probe on a very good day, not the new working weight** — he flagged the depth shortened slightly up there ('could go deeper'), and this program's standard is range first. The floor rising is the story; 80-85 stays the honest working set. **He confirmed depth at 80 is still improving week to week — so the depth lever is NOT spent, and the working set should not move up while it's still paying.**

**Thursday's conditioning cost Friday nothing — 'thought i'd be wiped out from the brutal complex but the opposite!'** That is the scheduling rule confirming itself from the other direction: Tuesday's eccentric experiment wrecked Wednesday's pull day, and Thursday's much harder session left Friday untouched. **Thursday remains the free slot for hard or experimental work.**

**He predicted the session from the morning flow and was right** — cossacks 'easy and flexy' meant he 'knew going in it would be good.' Worth keeping as a readiness read: the morning flow is already a daily movement screen, and it is more informative than sleep quality has been (W24D5 was bad sleep and a great day).

**The incline RDL's variable is where the weight sits, not what it weighs.** He jumped 55 → 70 and immediately found the load depends on holding position: arms straight and the weight further out felt like less; clamped tight to the chest 'definitely more.' Gravity is vertical, so hanging the plate lower changes nothing — what changes the lever is how HIGH on the torso it sits. **The cleaner progression is a single 45 held high at the collarbones or behind the head, not two plates he cannot keep in place.**

**Bulgarian right-leg fade did not recur, and the psoas spasms are gone.** Two standing concerns closed out in one session: 'no dying today' on the leg that died from rep one in W24, and 'i guess im not getting those psoas spazzes anymore.' Don't carry either forward as a watchpoint without new evidence.

**Both hip machines have numbers now and he wants them kept: adduction 290 (top of the stack), abduction 210 with a slow eccentric.** The adduction machine is already maxed out, so its only remaining lever is tempo — which is fine for a maintenance lift. Start abduction at 210 and adduction at 290 next time.

**The seated leg curl has been broken two weeks running and the Nordic fallback works.** 3 × 5 eccentric-only, done as written, 'these are hard!' — top of the rep range on the first honest attempt. **Promote the Nordic from fallback to the default knee-flexion slot** until the machine comes back, and note that it needs no equipment, which makes it the one legs-day lift that survives the interim period intact.

**DECIDED: the incline RDL goes back to a single 45 held HIGH — his call, *'good idea; lets experiment with these for next time using the 45.'*** Hold height (chest → collarbones → behind the head) is the progression on this lift now, not the plate.

**Calf raise tempo is ratcheting on its own — *'i'm just doing these slower and slower.'*** Same 4 plates for weeks, getting harder by tempo alone. Nothing to prescribe; just don't reset it by writing a number.
